To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the HINT database of manually curated protein-protein interactions can be used to expand a gene set by identifying network-based similarities among the genes, and 2) the expanded gene set can be used as a signature for the classification in an independent dataset of breast cancer metastatic patients.

(1) the use of a biological network to enrich gene signatures is a promising method for the identification of biomarkers for cancer metastases; and (2) the use of an independent test dataset is necessary for the validation of any such gene signature.

we present a novel method that uses a biological network to expand an initial gene set and then uses the resulting network as a gene signature for the prediction of metastasis in breast cancer patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of biological knowledge and gene expression data to improve the predictive power of gene signatures for the classification of cancerous diseases.
the integration of the biological network information into the process of biomarker discovery and the validation of the results.
the integration of network based information in gene signatures for cancer classification.

this method is a promising approach for the discovery of gene signatures for the classification of metastatic breast cancer cases.

our approach is able to enrich the initial gene signature with additional genes, and the resulting network is able to classify the metastatic cases in an independent dataset, with an accuracy of 80% and a precision of 90% (sensitivity of 80%).
